project.name: dotfiles
project.description: Personal dotfiles for mryfmo managed with chezmoi, with setup scripts for macOS, Ubuntu Desktop, and Ubuntu Server covering zsh, sheldon, starship, mise, and Claude Code/Codex agent tooling. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: cli.py
nodes.summary: Command-line interface for CompactionDB: an argparse front end exposing ledger queries (recent, prompts, search, files, sessions), recovery/probe/recall rendering, maintenance (drain, verify, prune, export, ingest), and durable-memory subcommands over ContextStore.
nodes.languageNotes: Dispatch is a long if/elif chain over argparse subcommand names; session scope defaults to 'session' so project-wide reads must be explicit.

nodes.name: build_parser
nodes.summary: Builds the contextdb argparse parser with all top-level subcommands and the nested 'memory' subcommand group (list, search, candidates, promote, add, retract, embed, semantic-search, compact).

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Main command dispatcher: resolves project paths and config, handles ingest/drain before opening the store, then executes ledger query, recovery, probe, recall, health, verify, prune, and export commands, delegating memory commands to _run_memory.

nodes.name: _run_memory
nodes.summary: Executes durable-memory subcommands: listing and searching current memories, promoting candidates, adding and retracting memories, building embeddings, semantic search, and rebuilding hierarchical memory blocks.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Process entry point that parses argv with build_parser and runs the selected command, returning an exit code.

nodes.name: probe.py
nodes.summary: Generates deterministic recovery probes with ground-truth answers (first failure, modified files, decisions, and other session facts) from a session's event ledger for evaluating compaction recovery quality.

nodes.name: generate_probes
nodes.summary: Queries the events table and current memories for a session and returns question/answer probe pairs whose answers are derived directly from the ledger.

nodes.name: recall.py
nodes.summary: Hybrid retrieval over the ledger: fuses FTS5 BM25 lexical scores with optional external-embedding semantic scores via a rho-weighted min-max normalized blend, then expands top hits with related events (tool-use pairs, neighbors) as a closure.
nodes.languageNotes: Score fusion is a convex combination rho*lexical + (1-rho)*semantic after min-max normalization of each signal.

nodes.name: normalize_scores
nodes.summary: Min-max normalizes a score map to [0, 1], mapping all-equal scores to 1.0.

nodes.name: _lexical
nodes.summary: Runs phrase-quoted FTS5 MATCH queries with negated bm25 scores over events and memories (optionally session-scoped) and returns keyed rows and raw lexical scores.

nodes.name: _semantic
nodes.summary: Returns semantic memory matches and scores when semantic search is enabled and embeddings exist, silently degrading to empty results on failure.

nodes.name: _closure
nodes.summary: Expands a hit event into related events (matching tool_use_id and adjacent events) with deduplication, labeling each with the relation path.

nodes.name: recall
nodes.summary: Top-level hybrid recall: combines normalized lexical and semantic scores with weight rho, ranks the top k records, and attaches closure context for event hits.

nodes.name: recovery.py
nodes.summary: Builds the bounded post-compaction recovery packet: a safety header with verification commands followed by sections for goal, file modifications, recent activity, decisions, open tasks, failures, and compact summary, all trimmed to a character budget.
nodes.languageNotes: Explicitly labels recovered log text as historical evidence, not instructions, and shell-quotes the session ID in suggested commands.

nodes.name: _detail
nodes.summary: Safely parses an event row's detail_json into a dict, returning an empty dict on invalid JSON or non-object values.

nodes.name: _modified_files
nodes.summary: Summarizes files changed in a session from the event_files table, rendering a budget-limited list of modified paths.

nodes.name: _render_packet
nodes.summary: Assembles the header and titled sections into a packet within the maximum length, middle-truncating the header and distributing the remaining budget across non-empty sections.

nodes.name: build_recovery_context
nodes.summary: Collects session prompts, events, files, memories, hierarchical project memory, failures, and the latest compact summary from ContextStore and renders them into the recovery packet.

nodes.name: semantic.py
nodes.summary: Optional semantic-search support: parses the semantic config section, calls a user-configured external embedding command over JSON stdin/stdout with strict response validation, and computes cosine similarity.
nodes.languageNotes: Rejects string commands so the embedder is always invoked as an argv array without a shell.

nodes.name: SemanticConfig
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass holding semantic-search settings: enabled flag, embedding command argv, model name, timeout, and batch size.

nodes.name: semantic_config
nodes.summary: Builds a SemanticConfig from the config dict with defaults and bounds, rejecting shell-string commands.

nodes.name: embed_texts
nodes.summary: Runs the external embedding command with texts as JSON input and validates the response model, vector count, finiteness, and consistent dimensionality.

nodes.name: cosine_similarity
nodes.summary: Computes cosine similarity between two vectors, returning -inf on length mismatch and 0.0 for zero-norm vectors.

nodes.name: storage.py
nodes.summary: SQLite persistence layer for CompactionDB: defines the schema (projects, sessions, events, event_files, memory candidates, memories, sources, embeddings, hierarchical blocks) with FTS5 indexes, and the ContextStore class for ingestion, memory lifecycle, search, integrity checks, pruning, and export.
nodes.languageNotes: Memories are append-only: retractions and supersessions add new rows instead of mutating existing ones; FTS5 tables are created opportunistically and degrade to tokenizer 'none'.

nodes.name: ContextStore
nodes.summary: Central store bound to project paths and config that owns the SQLite connection, schema, event insertion, durable-memory add/retract/promote, hierarchical memory blocks, lexical and semantic search, health, hash verification, pruning, and export.

nodes.name: connect
nodes.summary: Opens the SQLite database with row factory and pragmas, initializing the schema and securing storage file permissions when requested.

nodes.name: _ensure_fts
nodes.summary: Creates the events_fts and memories_fts FTS5 virtual tables when available, recording the tokenizer or 'none' when FTS5 is unsupported.

nodes.name: insert_event
nodes.summary: Idempotently inserts a redacted hook event with file references, upserts its session, indexes it in FTS, extracts memory candidates, and rebuilds memory blocks when memories changed.

nodes.name: _upsert_session
nodes.summary: Inserts or updates the sessions row with first/last timestamps, counters, and lifecycle metadata derived from an event.

nodes.name: _insert_candidates
nodes.summary: Stores memory candidates extracted from an event and auto-promotes explicit marker candidates into durable memories.

nodes.name: add_memory
nodes.summary: Validates and inserts a durable memory with scope, kind, fingerprint deduplication, supersession checks, provenance sources, and FTS indexing.

nodes.name: retract_memory
nodes.summary: Appends a retraction memory that supersedes a target memory and rebuilds project memory blocks.

nodes.name: current_memories
nodes.summary: Returns active, non-superseded memories for a project, optionally filtered by session and project-scope inclusion.

nodes.name: rebuild_memory_blocks
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the hierarchical project-memory projection by pairwise compressing leaf memory summaries into higher-level blocks.

nodes.name: hierarchical_memory_context
nodes.summary: Renders memory context lines from the block hierarchy plus current memories for inclusion in recovery packets.

nodes.name: search_events
nodes.summary: Searches event summaries and details via FTS5 with a LIKE fallback, optionally restricted to one session.

nodes.name: search_memories
nodes.summary: Searches current memories via FTS5 or LIKE fallback, returning only non-superseded rows.

nodes.name: promote_candidate
nodes.summary: Promotes an unpromoted memory candidate into a durable memory at the requested scope and links the candidate to it.

nodes.name: index_memory_embeddings
nodes.summary: Computes and stores external embeddings for current memories in configured batches, skipping ones already embedded for the model.

nodes.name: semantic_search_memories
nodes.summary: Embeds a query and ranks current memories by cosine similarity against stored embeddings.

nodes.name: health
nodes.summary: Reports database health: SQLite integrity, schema version, row counts, and FTS tokenizer status.

nodes.name: verify_hashes
nodes.summary: Verifies stored event detail hashes against recomputed SHA-256 digests and reports mismatches.

nodes.name: prune_expired
nodes.summary: Deletes expired or older-than-N-days raw events and their FTS rows while leaving durable memories intact.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Defines CompactionDB's DEFAULT_CONFIG (storage, capture, redaction, memory, recovery, recall, semantic, operations) and loads, deep-merges, validates, and persists the per-project JSON config.

nodes.name: validate_config
nodes.summary: Validates the merged config: config version, positive integer/number bounds for storage, capture, recovery, and recall keys, allowed SQLite journal/synchronous modes, and the semantic command shape.

nodes.name: load_config
nodes.summary: Loads the project config file, deep-merging user overrides onto DEFAULT_CONFIG and validating the result; optionally writes a default config with owner-only permissions when it is missing.

nodes.name: write_default_config
nodes.summary: Atomically writes the pretty-printed DEFAULT_CONFIG to the given path.

nodes.name: hook.py
nodes.summary: Claude Code lifecycle hook entry point for CompactionDB: reads the hook payload from stdin, normalizes it into an event, writes it to the durable spool, and opportunistically drains the spool into SQLite; at SessionEnd it also prunes expired events, old error-log lines, and quarantined files.

nodes.name: process_payload
nodes.summary: Normalizes one hook payload, spools it, and drains the spool with a non-blocking writer lock; on session_end it runs retention pruning of the store, error log, and quarantine directory, recording any failure to the error log.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that parses the JSON hook payload from stdin, validates it is an object, and delegates to process_payload, logging parse errors instead of failing the hook.

nodes.name: paths.py
nodes.summary: Resolves the CompactionDB project root and builds the frozen ProjectPaths layout (state, spool, quarantine, health, DB, config, lock, error log), including a race-safe persistent per-project UUID.

nodes.name: ProjectPaths
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass holding every CompactionDB path for a project plus its project_id; ensure() creates the state and spool directories with 0700 permissions.

nodes.name: resolve_project_root
nodes.summary: Resolves the project root from an explicit argument, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, the payload cwd, or the process cwd.

nodes.name: _load_or_create_project_id
nodes.summary: Reads and validates the stored project UUID, or creates it with an exclusive write and bounded retry loop so concurrent hooks agree on one ID.

nodes.name: project_paths
nodes.summary: Factory that builds a ProjectPaths for the resolved root, attaches the persistent project_id, and ensures the directory layout exists.

nodes.name: recover_hook.py
nodes.summary: Post-compaction recovery hook: drains pending spool events, builds a bounded recovery packet from the SQLite store, emits it as hook additionalContext JSON, and records a RecoveryInjected event.

nodes.name: _record_recovery_injected
nodes.summary: Normalizes and spools a synthetic RecoveryInjected event carrying the injected packet, logging any failure without raising.

nodes.name: recovery_output
nodes.summary: Loads config, drains the spool, builds the recovery context for the session from ContextStore, records the injection, and returns the hookSpecificOutput payload.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that reads the hook payload from stdin, calls recovery_output, and prints the JSON result, recording errors instead of failing the hook.

nodes.name: spool.py
nodes.summary: Durable file-based event spool for CompactionDB: writes each event as an exclusive JSON envelope, and drains envelopes into the SQLite ContextStore under a cross-platform single-writer lock, quarantining malformed records and logging errors to a JSONL log.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses fcntl.flock on POSIX and msvcrt.locking on Windows behind one context-manager lock; spool unlink failures are safe because event UUIDs make replay idempotent.

nodes.name: validate_ingestion_source
nodes.summary: Validates an ingestion-source label against a strict lowercase slug regex, rejecting anything else.

nodes.name: DrainResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass reporting a drain run: whether the lock was acquired and counts of processed, inserted, duplicate, quarantined, and remaining spool files plus any error.

nodes.name: WriterLock
nodes.summary: Context-manager file lock enforcing a single SQLite writer, with blocking or non-blocking acquisition with timeout via fcntl or msvcrt and PID stamping of the lock file.

nodes.name: record_error
nodes.summary: Appends a structured error record (UTC timestamp, stage, PID, exception type/message, extra context) to the project's JSONL error log.

nodes.name: spool_event
nodes.summary: Writes a normalized event into the incoming spool directory as a uniquely named JSON envelope created exclusively, optionally tagged with a validated ingestion source.

nodes.name: drain_spool
nodes.summary: Acquires the writer lock and ingests a batch of spooled envelopes into ContextStore, quarantining invalid records, counting duplicates, stopping on SQLite errors, and returning a DrainResult.

nodes.name: memory.py
nodes.summary: Heuristic memory-candidate extractor for CompactionDB: turns normalized hook events (post-compact summaries, explicit [memory:...] markers, keyword-bearing prompts and assistant messages) into scored MemoryCandidate records, plus a line compressor for recovery packets.
nodes.languageNotes: Frozen dataclass with a computed @property fingerprint; bilingual (English/Japanese) keyword and kind-alias tables drive regex-based sentence scoring.

nodes.name: MemoryCandidate
nodes.summary: Immutable dataclass describing a proposed durable memory (kind, content, scope, confidence, salience, reason, explicit flag) with a SHA-256 fingerprint over kind and normalized content for deduplication.

nodes.name: extract_candidates
nodes.summary: Derives memory candidates from a normalized event: PostCompact summaries become session-scoped candidates, explicit [memory:kind] markers in prompts are captured with high confidence, and remaining sentences are scored against bilingual keyword tables for constraints, decisions, preferences, and open tasks.

nodes.name: compress_lines
nodes.summary: Splits lines on pipes/newlines, deduplicates parts by normalized fingerprint, and joins them with ' | ', keeping roughly 40% head and 60% tail around an ellipsis marker when over the limit.

nodes.name: normalize.py
nodes.summary: Converts raw Claude Code hook payloads into CompactionDB's canonical event record: maps hook names to event types, sanitizes the payload through redaction before it touches disk, builds summaries and bounded detail JSON, extracts project-relative file references, hashes inputs/outputs, and attaches memory candidates.
nodes.languageNotes: Security-by-ordering: sanitize_payload runs first so no unredacted data reaches the spool or ledger.

nodes.name: _tool_summary
nodes.summary: Builds a one-line 'Tool succeeded/failed: subject' summary, using the Bash command or the first of file_path/path/query/pattern/url/description from the tool input (falling back to canonical JSON) and appending any error.

nodes.name: _relative_path
nodes.summary: Resolves a raw path against the project root and returns it project-relative when inside the root, otherwise the resolved absolute path.

nodes.name: _extract_file_refs
nodes.summary: Collects deduplicated, project-relative file references from tool input/response (and FileChanged events), tagging each with an operation (write, edit, read, search, reference) by tool name and a restricted/internal sensitivity.

nodes.name: encode_detail
nodes.summary: Serializes event detail to JSON bounded by max_chars, shrinking per-field truncation budgets iteratively and falling back to a preview (or bare metadata) annotated with the original length and SHA-256.

nodes.name: normalize_hook_payload
nodes.summary: Main normalization entry: sanitizes a hook payload, derives event type, success flag, summary, and per-event normalized detail, then assembles the full event dict with hashes, sensitivity, retention expiry, file references, and memory candidates.

nodes.name: redaction.py
nodes.summary: Secret-redaction layer for CompactionDB: regex patterns for high-signal credentials (private keys, API tokens, JWTs, credential assignments), sensitive-path detection, sensitive-key masking, and recursive payload sanitization driven by config.
nodes.languageNotes: Closures inside redact_text capture the category loop variable per pattern to record redaction counts on a shared RedactionReport.

nodes.name: RedactionReport
nodes.summary: Mutable dataclass tallying redaction count, triggered categories, and whether a sensitive path was involved.

nodes.name: is_sensitive_path
nodes.summary: Classifies a path as sensitive based on sensitive directories, file names (.env*), suffixes, and credential-like name tokens.

nodes.name: redact_text
nodes.summary: Applies each credential regex to a string, substituting a templated [REDACTED:kind] marker while preserving assignment prefixes and basic-auth URL structure.

nodes.name: find_paths
nodes.summary: Recursively walks dicts and lists to collect string values stored under path-like keys.

nodes.name: redact_value
nodes.summary: Recursively redacts a JSON-like value: masks sensitive keys, suppresses file content fields when required, redacts text patterns, and truncates long strings.

nodes.name: sanitize_payload
nodes.summary: Top-level sanitizer that reads redaction/capture config, detects sensitive paths, decides content suppression, and returns the redacted payload with its RedactionReport.

nodes.name: util.py
nodes.summary: Shared low-level helpers for CompactionDB: UTC timestamps, canonical JSON and hashing, text truncation and fingerprint normalization, permission-safe directory creation, and durable file writes (exclusive, atomic with fsync, JSONL append).
nodes.languageNotes: Durability via os.open flags (O_EXCL, O_APPEND), explicit fsync of both file and parent directory, and os.replace for atomic rename.

nodes.name: utc_now
nodes.summary: Returns the current timezone-aware UTC datetime.

nodes.name: utc_iso
nodes.summary: Formats a datetime as millisecond-precision ISO-8601 UTC with a Z suffix.

nodes.name: epoch_ms
nodes.summary: Returns a datetime as integer epoch milliseconds.

nodes.name: canonical_json
nodes.summary: Serializes a value to compact, key-sorted, non-ASCII-preserving JSON for stable hashing.

nodes.name: pretty_json
nodes.summary: Serializes a value to indented, key-sorted JSON for human display.

nodes.name: sha256_text
nodes.summary: Returns the hex SHA-256 digest of a UTF-8 string.

nodes.name: stable_id
nodes.summary: Derives a deterministic identifier by SHA-256 hashing unit-separator-joined parts and truncating to a given length.

nodes.name: one_line
nodes.summary: Collapses any value to a whitespace-normalized single line capped at a limit.

nodes.name: truncate_middle
nodes.summary: Truncates text to a limit by keeping head and tail with a marker in the middle.

nodes.name: normalize_for_fingerprint
nodes.summary: Casefolds and whitespace-normalizes text for fingerprint comparisons.

nodes.name: ensure_dir
nodes.summary: Creates a directory tree if missing and applies restrictive permissions.

nodes.name: safe_chmod
nodes.summary: Applies chmod while ignoring platforms or filesystems that reject it.

nodes.name: _fsync_directory
nodes.summary: Fsyncs a directory to make renames and creations durable, tolerating platforms without directory fsync.

nodes.name: write_text_exclusive
nodes.summary: Creates a new file exclusively (O_EXCL) with restricted mode, writes text, and fsyncs file and parent directory.

nodes.name: write_json_exclusive
nodes.summary: Writes a value as canonical JSON to a newly created file via write_text_exclusive.

nodes.name: atomic_write_text
nodes.summary: Atomically replaces a file by writing to a temp file, fsyncing, renaming with os.replace, and fsyncing the directory.

nodes.name: append_jsonl
nodes.summary: Appends one canonical-JSON line to a JSONL file using O_APPEND with restricted permissions.

nodes.name: parse_utc
nodes.summary: Parses an ISO-8601 string (accepting Z) into a UTC datetime.

nodes.name: chunks
nodes.summary: Yields fixed-size lists from an iterable.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Single-stage Ubuntu 24.04 image that provisions a passwordless-sudo user (default mryfmo, UID/GID 1000) with the Asia/Tokyo timezone and installs chezmoi, giving a clean sandbox for applying and testing the dotfiles setup.
nodes.languageNotes: The user-creation RUN step reuses any existing group/user at the requested GID/UID (renaming it with groupmod/usermod) instead of failing, which matters on Ubuntu 24.04 images that already ship an 'ubuntu' user at UID 1000.

nodes.name: ubuntu
nodes.summary: The sole build stage, based on ubuntu:24.04, which installs curl, git, sudo, tzdata, parallel, build-essential and ca-certificates, then sets the working directory to ~/.local/share/chezmoi and installs the chezmoi binary into /usr/local/bin.

nodes.name: agent-assets.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that validates agent, MCP, plugin, and skill assets with scripts/validate-agent-assets.py on pushes/PRs to main, and on a weekly schedule also checks upstream Codex/Claude Code documentation links and current npm package versions for drift.

nodes.name: docs.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that deploys the project documentation site via `make deploy` (mkdocs) on pushes to main touching docs-relevant paths, installing tools through uv and mise and committing as github-actions[bot].

nodes.name: macos.yaml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that bootstraps the dotfiles on a macos-14 runner with setup.sh (including private dotfiles via deploy key), verifies that a rerun rejects local drift, runs and publishes a setup benchmark, and checks installed files with the common and macOS Bats suites.
nodes.languageNotes: Every step is gated on repository-secret presence flags (HAS_*) computed in job env, so forks and secretless contexts skip cleanly instead of failing.

nodes.name: remote.yaml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow testing the snippet-style bootstrap of setup.sh against the checked-out commit across Ubuntu client/server and macOS client, using an isolated HOME and sentinel files to prove unmanaged files keep their contents and modes; a second job optionally exercises private restoration when secrets exist.

nodes.name: test.yaml
nodes.summary: Required unit-test workflow that always reports status, uses a changes job to decide whether to run the full Ubuntu/macOS client/server matrix (shfmt, ShellCheck, Python unit tests, offline statusline smoke test, chezmoi fixture apply, Bats with bashcov coverage uploaded to Codecov) and a separate Nix flake evaluation job.
nodes.languageNotes: Avoids workflow-level path filters so required checks never stay pending; relevance is computed in-job via git diff and exposed as job outputs gating later steps.

nodes.name: ubuntu.yaml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that bootstraps the dotfiles on Ubuntu for server and client systems with setup.sh, verifies rerun drift rejection on ~/.zprofile, and validates installed files with the common and tag-filtered Ubuntu Bats suites.

nodes.name: config.json
nodes.summary: Understand-Anything project settings selecting English output and enabling automatic incremental graph updates.

nodes.name: fingerprints.json
nodes.summary: Generated per-file fingerprint index (content hash, functions, classes, imports, exports, line counts) pinned to commit 935e198, used by Understand-Anything to detect changed files for incremental re-analysis.
nodes.languageNotes: Machine-generated JSON keyed by project-relative path; not meant for hand editing.

nodes.name: knowledge-graph.json
nodes.summary: Generated repo-local knowledge graph of the dotfiles project (870 nodes, 1333 edges, 9 architectural layers, 15-step tour) that agents query before repo-wide exploration.
nodes.languageNotes: Top-level keys: version, project, nodes, edges, layers, tour; the project block records analyzedAt and gitCommitHash for staleness checks.

nodes.name: meta.json
nodes.summary: Records when the knowledge graph was last analyzed, the analyzed git commit hash (935e198), and the analyzed file count (424), used to judge graph staleness against HEAD.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Canonical agent instruction file for all runtimes, covering chezmoi repository context, ADH distribution boundaries, comment and git/PR policy, bats test policy, agent review evidence, and standing auditor and code-review rules.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Claude-only shim that imports AGENTS.md and carries the CompactionDB-managed block describing context recovery and durable memory CLI commands.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: Top-level task runner defining lifecycle targets for the dotfiles: Docker test container, chezmoi setup/init/update (public and private sources, pinned mise installs, agent asset refresh, Herdr reload, agmsg bootstrap), doctor/upgrade, unit tests, agent-asset validation, crit review guard, and MkDocs docs build/serve/deploy.
nodes.languageNotes: Recipes use multi-line shell with doubled $$ escaping and .PHONY targets; 'update' guards git pull behind branch/upstream/cleanliness checks before chezmoi apply.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Main project documentation covering the chezmoi-managed dotfiles overview, macOS/Ubuntu setup, lifecycle Make commands, MkDocs documentation generation, agent review and permission assets, agmsg and Herdr/Ghostty agent workspaces, local/Docker/Bats testing, Codecov, and tips.

nodes.name: codecov.yml
nodes.summary: Codecov configuration that ignores the config itself and Codex skill assets under home/dot_agents/skills, and sets an auto project coverage target with a 1% threshold.

nodes.name: mise.toml
nodes.summary: Empty repository-local mise configuration containing only a [tools] table; actual tool pins live in the managed home/dot_mise config.

nodes.name: mkdocs.yml
nodes.summary: MkDocs site configuration for the generated shell-automation reference docs, using the Material theme, search and toc-md catalog plugins, extra CSS, and pymdownx code-highlighting extensions.

nodes.name: renovate.json
nodes.summary: Renovate dependency-update configuration enabling GitHub Actions, mise, and regex managers for agent-config.yaml GitHub-release and crates.io pins, with a weekly schedule, grouped minor/patch updates, dashboard-approval gating for pins that make upgrade must recompute, and an fd hold.

nodes.name: setup.sh
nodes.summary: Remote bootstrap script for macOS and Ubuntu that installs Homebrew (checksum-pinned) on macOS, downloads and checksum-verifies a pinned chezmoi release, runs chezmoi init/update, refuses to apply over local drift or outside RUNNER_TEMP in CI, then applies the dotfiles.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash with set -Eeuo pipefail, shdoc annotations, and an accumulating EXIT trap (at_exit) for temp-file cleanup.

nodes.name: fetch_url
nodes.summary: Downloads a URL to stdout, preferring curl and falling back to wget.

nodes.name: fetch_file
nodes.summary: Downloads a URL to a file, preferring curl and falling back to wget.

nodes.name: verify_sha256
nodes.summary: Verifies a file against an expected SHA-256 digest, failing on missing or mismatched checksums.

nodes.name: keepalive_sudo_linux
nodes.summary: Requests sudo up front on Linux and keeps the timestamp alive with a background loop.

nodes.name: keepalive_sudo_macos
nodes.summary: Requests sudo up front on macOS via /usr/bin/sudo and keeps the timestamp alive without touching Keychain.

nodes.name: keepalive_sudo
nodes.summary: Dispatches to the OS-specific sudo keepalive once per run, guarded by an environment flag.

nodes.name: initialize_os_macos
nodes.summary: Installs Homebrew non-interactively from a pinned, checksum-verified installer when absent and loads brew shellenv from the detected prefix.

nodes.name: initialize_os_env
nodes.summary: Dispatches OS initialization by uname result, exiting on unsupported platforms.

nodes.name: run_chezmoi
nodes.summary: Fetches and verifies the platform-specific pinned chezmoi binary, runs init and update, strips encrypted files in CI/non-TTY, aborts on local drift or unsafe CI HOME, applies the target state, and removes the temporary binary.

nodes.name: initialize_dotfiles
nodes.summary: Starts sudo keepalive in interactive sessions and runs the chezmoi bootstrap.

nodes.name: restart_shell_system
nodes.summary: Reads the chezmoi system data and re-execs zsh for client or bash for server as a login shell.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Script entry point that prints the logo, initializes the OS environment, and bootstraps the dotfiles.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Architecture guide for the shared AI-agent asset directory: declares agent-config.yaml as the single source of truth, lists the generated Codex/Claude Code files, sets MCP parity and secret-free policies, and documents the generate/check/validate/runtime-doctor commands.

nodes.name: agent-config.yaml
nodes.summary: Canonical hand-edited manifest for Codex and Claude Code: model profiles (express/standard/review/deep/security/audit/adh), herdr worker kind/profile/worktree, Codex and Claude settings, permissions and hooks, plugins, disabled-by-default MCP servers, and managed tool assets such as mise, agmsg, crit, and understand-anything.
nodes.languageNotes: YAML manifest rendered into agent-native TOML/JSON/env files by a generator script rather than consumed directly at runtime.

nodes.name: model-profiles.env
nodes.summary: Generated shell fragment sourced by agent launchers (herdr-agents, agent-fanout) that exports the interactive profile, herdr worker kind/profile/worktree, and per-profile Claude/Codex CLI argument strings.

nodes.name: permgate-policy.yaml
nodes.summary: permgate schema-v2 policy (JSON-in-YAML) defining shadow-only LLM classifier providers, deterministic deny/workspace-write/allow decision layers, read-deny patterns for secrets, whitelisted read-only categories with regex allow patterns, a root-rm deny rule, and enablement latency thresholds.
nodes.languageNotes: Written as JSON syntax inside a .yaml file; permgate loads it with json.loads, so it must remain valid JSON.

nodes.name: modify_private_config.toml
nodes.summary: chezmoi modify_ script (Python) that renders the managed Codex baseline from .chezmoitemplates/codex-config-managed.toml and merges it into ~/.codex/config.toml, preserving Codex-owned runtime tables (hooks.state, marketplaces, tui.model_availability_nux, projects) and unmanaged user tables.
nodes.languageNotes: Despite the .toml target name, this is a Python chezmoi modify_ script: chezmoi pipes the current file on stdin and writes stdout back; it substitutes chezmoi template variables itself via CHEZMOI_* env vars.

nodes.name: common.toml

nodes.name: macos.toml

nodes.name: cache.sh

nodes.name: cuda.sh
nodes.summary: Sourced zsh snippet for server shells that sets CUDA_HOME, appends the CUDA bin directory to the deduplicated path array, and extends LD_LIBRARY_PATH with the CUDA lib64 directory.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses zsh-specific `typeset -gU path` to keep the path array unique and the `(N-/)` glob qualifier so the CUDA bin entry is only added when the directory exists.

nodes.name: history.sh
nodes.summary: Sourced bash snippet that shares shell history across concurrent sessions by registering a PROMPT_COMMAND hook that deduplicates and reloads ~/.bash_history, with a sed-based tac fallback.
nodes.languageNotes: The `tac` fallback uses the classic sed idiom `1!G;h;$!d` to reverse lines, and `awk '!a[$0]++'` removes duplicates while keeping the most recent occurrence.

nodes.name: share_history
nodes.summary: PROMPT_COMMAND hook that appends session history, rewrites ~/.bash_history with duplicates removed (keeping latest entries), then clears and reloads the in-memory history.

nodes.name: ssh_agent.sh
nodes.summary: Sheldon-sourced bash snippet that starts ssh-agent and loads the default ed25519 key when readable, printing guidance to stderr otherwise, then removes its helper function from the shell.
nodes.languageNotes: Designed to be sourced into an interactive shell: it avoids strict shell options, fails soft with `|| return 0`, and unsets its helper function after running to keep the namespace clean.

nodes.name: _dotfiles_start_ssh_agent
nodes.summary: Evaluates ssh-agent output to start the agent and runs ssh-add on ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 when readable, reporting failures or a missing key on stderr without aborting the shell.

nodes.name: chezmoi_private.sh
nodes.summary: Installer step that initializes and applies the private chezmoi source (dotfiles-private) over SSH into dedicated source/config paths, warning instead of failing when unavailable; also provides an uninstall routine.

nodes.name: install_chezmoi_private
nodes.summary: Runs chezmoi init --apply --ssh with the private source and config paths, emitting a warning and continuing if initialization fails.

nodes.name: gh_extensions.sh
nodes.summary: Installer step that activates mise and installs the configured GitHub CLI extensions (e.g. gh-poi) idempotently, skipping with a warning when gh is not authenticated.

nodes.name: install_gh_extensions
nodes.summary: Checks gh auth status, then installs each configured extension not already present in gh extension list.

nodes.name: mise.sh
nodes.summary: Installer step that downloads a pinned standalone mise release for the current OS/arch, verifies it against the upstream SHA256 manifest, installs it atomically, and runs locked mise installs for node, statusline tools, agent CLIs, and the remaining repository tools.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a subshell-bodied function `name() ( ... )` so the EXIT trap cleaning temp files is scoped to that function; the extraction script did not detect this form, so it was added manually.

nodes.name: mise_artifact
nodes.summary: Maps uname OS/architecture to the matching mise release tarball name, failing on unsupported platforms.

nodes.name: verify_mise_archive
nodes.summary: Looks up the expected checksum for an artifact in a SHASUMS256 manifest and compares it with sha256sum or shasum output, failing on missing or mismatched checksums.

nodes.name: _install_mise_binary
nodes.summary: Downloads the pinned mise tarball and checksum manifest to a temp dir, verifies and extracts it, and atomically moves the binary into the install path with trap-based cleanup.

nodes.name: run_mise_install
nodes.summary: Trusts the local mise config and runs staged locked installs: node, statusline npm tools, agent CLIs with a release-age bypass, then all remaining tools with a minimum release-age floor.

nodes.name: sheldon.sh
nodes.summary: Installer step that builds the pinned Sheldon zsh plugin manager from crates.io via mise-provided cargo with locked dependencies, then installs the binary atomically into ~/.local/bin.

nodes.name: install_sheldon
nodes.summary: Runs cargo install --locked for the pinned sheldon version into a temp root through mise exec, then atomically installs the binary with trap-based cleanup.
nodes.languageNotes: Subshell-bodied function scoping its EXIT trap; added manually because the extraction script missed this form.

nodes.name: brew.sh

nodes.languageNotes: Installer commit and checksum are rendered from agent-config.yaml; the download runs in a subshell with an EXIT trap to clean up the temp file.

nodes.name: install_homebrew
nodes.summary: Downloads the pinned Homebrew install.sh to a temp file, verifies its SHA-256 against the expected digest, and runs it non-interactively only when brew is absent.

nodes.name: command_line_tool.sh

nodes.name: install_command_line_tool

nodes.name: main

nodes.name: zed.sh

nodes.languageNotes: install_pinned_zed uses a subshell function body `( ... )` so its EXIT trap cleans up temp files without leaking into the caller.

nodes.name: zed_artifact
nodes.summary: Maps uname -m to the Zed Linux tarball name and prints it with the matching pinned SHA256, failing on unsupported architectures.

nodes.name: install_pinned_zed

nodes.name: apparmor_userns.sh

nodes.languageNotes: Every path is overridable through environment variables (sysctl, bwrap, profile source/target), which makes the script testable without touching /etc or /proc.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Checks skip_reason and either prints why the bwrap userns profile is unnecessary or installs and reloads it.

nodes.languageNotes: install_aws_cli uses a subshell body `function f() ( ... )` so its EXIT trap cleans the temp dir without leaking into the caller; the extractor missed it for that reason.

nodes.name: aws_cli_url
nodes.summary: Builds the versioned official AWS CLI archive URL for x86_64 or aarch64, failing on unsupported architectures.

nodes.name: verify_aws_cli_version
nodes.summary: Checks that an executable exists and that its --version output reports exactly the pinned aws-cli version.

nodes.name: install_aws_cli
nodes.summary: Downloads the archive and signature to a temp dir, validates the signing key fingerprint, validity, and expiry, verifies the signature with gpgv, checks the staged binary version, then runs the bundled installer and verifies the result.

nodes.name: dependencies.sh
nodes.summary: Installs the base Ubuntu apt toolchain the dotfiles need (build tools, git, curl, zsh, gpg, etc.), bootstrapping sudo on minimal containers and only installing packages dpkg-query reports as missing; also offers an uninstall path that keeps sudo and git.

nodes.name: run_apt_get

nodes.name: install_apt_packages

nodes.name: uninstall_apt_packages

nodes.name: ssh.sh

nodes.name: setup_timezone.sh
nodes.summary: Ubuntu server setup script that sets the system timezone to Asia/Tokyo by linking /etc/localtime and writing /etc/timezone, then installs tzdata non-interactively.

nodes.name: ssh_server.sh

nodes.name: starship.sh

nodes.languageNotes: install_starship uses a subshell function body `( ... )` so its EXIT trap cleans up temp files without leaking into the caller's shell; the binary is staged in the destination directory and moved into place for an atomic replace.

nodes.name: configure_accept_env
nodes.summary: Merges proxy-related environment variable names into a single deduplicated AcceptEnv line in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.

nodes.name: setup_sshd

nodes.name: starship_artifact
nodes.summary: Maps uname -m to the matching musl Starship release archive name, failing on unsupported architectures.

nodes.name: install_starship

nodes.name: 001-contain-starship-cleanup.md
nodes.summary: P0 hardening plan (audit finding F01) that stops the Ubuntu Server Starship uninstall and its Bats teardown from recursively deleting the shared ~/.local/bin directory, restricting removal to the installed Starship binary under an isolated test HOME.
nodes.languageNotes: Plans follow a fixed executor template: drift check, measured file:line current state, atomic A-numbered tasks, STOP conditions, and a 安全回帰 (safety regression) section.

nodes.name: 002-make-review-evidence-non-vacuous.md
nodes.summary: P0 plan (finding F02) that tightens the require-crit-review guard so AGENT_REVIEWED receipts reject null or empty Crit JSON and require a non-empty resolved-record shape, with matching unit tests and operator documentation updates.

nodes.name: 003-make-bootstrap-safe-and-publicly-testable.md
nodes.summary: Five-phase P1 plan (findings F03, F08, F09, F11, F14) making the public bootstrap dependency-correct on Ubuntu via Debian package state, supporting wget-only fetches, replacing forced chezmoi overwrites with preview and recovery, testing the PR checkout without secrets in CI, and validating the Linux system role before persistence.

nodes.name: 004-harden-and-lock-the-supply-chain.md
nodes.summary: Five-phase P1 supply-chain plan (findings F04, F05, F06, F10, F18) that checksum-verifies remote installers, pins GitHub Actions to commit SHAs with least-privilege permissions, locks mise and Sheldon versions, removes live GitHub API calls from chezmoi externals, and updates and CI-evaluates the Nix flake.

nodes.name: 005-make-runtime-health-and-verification-truthful.md
nodes.summary: Seven-phase P1 plan (findings F07, F12, F13, F15-F17, F19) that makes agent run artifacts private and ignored, gives doctor and upgrade truthful nonzero exit codes, restarts stale Herdr Yazi file panes, reloads Herdr after config updates, replaces placeholder platform Bats files, removes rolling npx from the statusline, and enforces ShellCheck in CI.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Index of the 2026-07 dotfiles production-hardening program: global execution rules, the phased order and DONE status of plans 001-005 with merge commits, a one-to-one mapping of audit findings F01-F19 to plan tasks, dependency rationale, and final acceptance criteria.

nodes.name: check-tools.sh

nodes.name: check_command

nodes.name: check_agmsg

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to see what this repository is: a chezmoi-managed dotfiles project that provisions macOS, Ubuntu Desktop (client) and Ubuntu Server (server) machines with zsh, sheldon, starship and mise, plus a substantial layer of Claude Code and Codex agent tooling. It introduces the one-line setup snippets, the Make lifecycle commands, the agent review and permission assets, and the Bats-based testing story that the rest of this tour walks through.

tour.title: Bootstrap Entry Point
tour.description: setup.sh is the real entry point: the README's curl snippet runs it, the Makefile depends on it, and three CI workflows trigger it. It installs checksum-pinned Homebrew on macOS, downloads and verifies a pinned chezmoi release, and refuses to apply over local drift before handing control to chezmoi. The .chezmoiroot marker then tells chezmoi that the source state lives under home/, and home/.chezmoi.yaml.tmpl resolves per-machine data such as the client/server role and whether the private layer is enabled.
tour.languageLesson: chezmoi encodes target attributes in source file names: dot_ becomes a leading dot, private_ sets 0600/0700 modes, executable_ sets the execute bit, symlink_ creates a symlink, modify_ runs a script that rewrites an existing target, and a .tmpl suffix renders the file through Go templates with the data from .chezmoi.yaml.tmpl.

tour.title: Selecting What Gets Applied
tour.description: With the machine role known from Step 2, chezmoi's control files decide what actually lands in $HOME. .chezmoiignore composes OS- and role-specific ignore fragments so a server never receives desktop files, .chezmoiexternal.yaml.tmpl pulls in external archives and repositories per platform, and .chezmoiremove deletes retired files from earlier generations of the setup. Together they make one source tree serve three very different machine types.

tour.title: Run-Once Installer Pipeline
tour.description: Files alone cannot install software, so chezmoi runs scripts from home/.chezmoiscripts; each is a thin run_once wrapper that includes the real logic from install/. The mise installer shows the house style: download a pinned release, verify it against an upstream SHA256 manifest, and install atomically, while brew.sh and the Ubuntu dependencies script prepare each platform. scripts/lib/installer-pins.sh centralizes pinned versions and checksums, a supply-chain posture you will see again in CI and tests.
tour.languageLesson: chezmoi orders scripts by name and prefix: run_once_before_* runs before files are written, plain run_once_* runs with them, and run_once_after_* runs after, while the NN numbers sort scripts within each phase. run_once_ scripts rerun only when their rendered content changes, so the included install/ script's hash effectively acts as a version.

tour.title: Shell Runtime
tour.description: Once tools are installed, the deployed shell files wire them together. dot_zshenv sets a deduplicated PATH with mise shims first for every zsh, including non-interactive SSH commands, while dot_zshrc activates mise, initializes sheldon plugins and wraps herdr. The sheldon template assembles client or server plugin sets, starship shows pending chezmoi updates in the prompt, and dot_mise/config.toml is the global tool manifest that pins runtimes, CLIs and the Claude Code and Codex agent CLIs.
tour.languageLesson: zsh reads .zshenv for every shell (interactive or not), .zprofile for login shells and .zshrc only for interactive shells. PATH belongs in .zshenv so scripts and remote commands see the same tools, while prompts and plugins belong in .zshrc.

tour.title: Agent Config Manifest
tour.description: The agent half of the repository is driven by one hand-edited file: agent-config.yaml, the most depended-upon node in the graph. It declares model profiles (express, standard, review, deep, security, audit), herdr worker settings, Claude Code and Codex permissions, hooks, plugins and MCP servers. The dot_agents README documents it as the single source of truth, model-profiles.env and the managed Codex baseline are rendered from it, and launchers such as agent-fanout consume those rendered profiles rather than hard-coding model flags.

tour.title: Rendering Agent Settings
tour.description: generate-agent-configs.py turns the manifest from Step 6 into concrete managed baselines for Claude Code and Codex. Because both tools also write their own runtime state into their config files, the repository does not overwrite them: chezmoi modify_ scripts merge the managed Claude settings baseline into settings.json and the Codex baseline into config.toml, preserving tool-owned tables such as enabled plugins, marketplaces and project trust. This is a deliberate design for managing files that another program also edits.
tour.languageLesson: A chezmoi modify_ script receives the current target file on stdin and must print the desired content on stdout. That makes it a merge hook: here Python scripts parse JSON or TOML, overlay the managed keys and emit the result, which is safer than templating a file the application rewrites at runtime.

tour.title: Agent Executables and Policy
tour.description: The configuration from Steps 6-7 comes alive through executables installed in ~/.local/bin. herdr-agents lays out a Claude Code orchestrator and Codex worker pane pair in separate git worktrees, agmsg-dispatch delivers messages between them and waits for read receipts, and permgate is a deterministic-first permission gate driven by permgate-policy.yaml, with LLM classifiers kept in shadow mode. The agmsg-orchestration rule describes the delegation protocol these tools implement.

tour.title: CompactionDB Event Capture
tour.description: CompactionDB is a Python package bundled in .claude/contextdb that gives agent sessions a durable memory across context compaction. The project .claude/settings.json registers contextdb_hook.py on every Claude Code lifecycle event, and that thin launcher delegates to hook.py. hook.py normalizes each payload into a canonical event, and normalize.py runs redaction.py over it so that secrets are masked before anything touches disk.
tour.languageLesson: Python's sys.path controls where import looks for modules. The hook launcher prepends the bundled package directory to sys.path and then imports contextdb.hook, a common way to ship a self-contained package alongside scripts without installing it into site-packages.

tour.title: CompactionDB Storage and Recovery
tour.description: Captured events from Step 9 are written as exclusive JSON envelopes to spool.py's file spool, then drained under a single-writer lock into the SQLite store defined in storage.py (with shared paths.py and util.py helpers underneath). After a compaction, recover_hook.py asks recovery.py to build a bounded packet of goals, modified files, decisions and failures and injects it back into the session. cli.py exposes the same store for queries, integrity checks, pruning and durable-memory management.
tour.languageLesson: SQLite's FTS5 extension provides full-text search tables with built-in BM25 ranking. Pairing a spool directory with a single-writer drain is a simple way to accept events from many concurrent hook processes without SQLite lock contention.

tour.title: Lifecycle and Maintenance Tooling
tour.description: The Makefile is the operator's front door: setup, update, doctor, upgrade, test, validate and docs targets all route through it and ultimately back to setup.sh from Step 2. update-agent-assets.sh converges what chezmoi cannot express as files (plugin marketplaces, pinned agent tools, gh extensions), validate-agent-assets.py checks the manifest and generated assets from Steps 6-7, check-agent-runtime.py reports drift in the live HOME, and require-crit-review.py blocks meaningful diffs without review evidence.
tour.languageLesson: Make targets that do not produce files should be declared .PHONY so Make always runs them. Here the Makefile works as a documented command catalogue for lifecycle actions rather than as a build graph.

tour.title: Behavioral Test Suites
tour.description: Tests come in two flavours. Bats suites check applied dotfiles and installer behaviour, with helpers.bash providing file-content, mode and idempotent-apply assertions and run_unit_test.sh selecting suites by OS and role. Python unittest suites cover the agent tooling, for example test_runtime_health.py for pinned, checksum-verified installs and upgrade reporting, and test_workflow_security.py for static policy over the CI workflows introduced in the next step.
tour.languageLesson: Bats (Bash Automated Testing System) wraps each @test block in a subshell and uses the run helper to capture $status and $output, so shell scripts can be tested with plain assertions such as [ "$status" -eq 0 ]. Per the repository policy these suites run in GitHub Actions rather than locally.

tour.title: CI and Test Sandbox
tour.description: GitHub Actions ties everything together. test.yaml is the required matrix across Ubuntu and macOS client/server (shfmt, ShellCheck, Python tests, Bats with bashcov coverage), macos.yaml and ubuntu.yaml bootstrap real runners with setup.sh and verify rerun drift protection, and remote.yaml proves the curl snippet leaves unmanaged files untouched. The Ubuntu 24.04 Dockerfile gives a local sandbox for applying the dotfiles the same way.
tour.languageLesson: Pinning third-party GitHub Actions to a full commit SHA instead of a tag prevents a moved or compromised tag from changing what runs in CI, and a minimal top-level permissions map limits the GITHUB_TOKEN. test_workflow_security.py from Step 12 enforces both rules.

tour.title: Rules and Agent Guidance
tour.description: Many design choices you have seen are codified as instructions for the agents that maintain this repository. AGENTS.md is the canonical instruction file for every runtime, covering chezmoi boundaries, git/PR policy and the standing audit rules, while CLAUDE.md is only a shim that imports it. Global rules such as model-selection.md explain why model IDs live only in agent-config.yaml (Step 6) and how the orchestrator, worker and auditor roles are split.

tour.title: Hardening History and Nix
tour.description: Finally, the plans directory records why the codebase looks the way it does: plans/README.md indexes a five-phase production-hardening program, and plan 004 explains the supply-chain pinning seen in Steps 4, 11 and 13. flake.nix and the nix-first architecture plan describe an opt-in Nix layer with Home Manager and nix-darwin outputs that deliberately keeps setup.sh and chezmoi authoritative, pointing at where the project may evolve next.
tour.languageLesson: A Nix flake pins every input (nixpkgs, Home Manager, nix-darwin) in flake.lock, so evaluation is reproducible; outputs such as homeConfigurations and darwinConfigurations describe whole user or system environments declaratively.
